conceptual assets.information: The byte-banked words written from bus request data and later returned for data-memory reads; processor and system data-memory operation depends on their contents.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The stored bytes can be exposed through rdata and bus_rsp_o.data at lines 75-78 and 129. The memory banks can be overwritten from bus_req_i.data on write requests at lines 61-74. The contents do not themselves gate a transfer or block operation in the shown RTL. No privileged mode, override, bypass or similar integration behavior acts on the contents.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue an unchecked write to overwrite a memory word and then issue a read to disclose or corrupt the stored data.

conceptual assets.information: The registered decision that enables or masks a memory-read value on the response data port; a normal read response depends on this gate.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: This control decision is written from the request strobe and read/write direction at line 124, so changing it changes whether the read response is enabled. When rden is not asserted, line 129 masks bus_rsp_o.data to zero and can withhold the required read data.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the request control fields so rden is cleared, causing valid memory-read data to be withheld.

conceptual assets.information: The address selecting which data-memory word is read or written; correct data-memory behavior depends on targeting the intended location. It is not returned by this unit.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The access address is control material driven into addr at line 113 and used to select memory locations for reads and writes at lines 63-78, so changing it can redirect an access to the wrong word.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter bus_req_i.addr so a write corrupts an unintended memory word or a read returns data from the wrong location.

considered, not kept.reason: bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.ben only qualify which memory access occurs at lines 61-74 and are access-command fields rather than independent information pieces.
bus_rsp_o.ack only repeats bus_req_i.stb at line 125, so it is a bus-handshake copy rather than an information asset of its own.
bus_rsp_o.err is tied to a constant at line 130 and carries no runtime information.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the logic at lines 26-27 and 120-125, and clocks and reset chains are excluded as conceptual assets.
DMEM_SIZE and the fixed alt_style_c choice at lines 23 and 36 only determine build-time memory structure and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
